# unslop

Unslop works like a designer doing a redline pass, one layer at a time, across the whole screen. It targets the usual tells of vibecoded UI: purple gradients, glows, gradient text, emoji labels, "New" badges, glossy blobs, uppercase tracked labels, pulsing elements and uneven spacing. It works on React, Tailwind, HTML and CSS, for dashboards, apps and landing pages.

The run starts by looking at the screen, from code, from a live page saved as a copy, or from a screenshot rebuilt as one static HTML file. It then audits every sign found, decides how much to change, and writes a five line direction: product, character, world, moments and signature. The direction is shown to the user before editing, and editing waits for the answer, unless the user already said to just do it.

The nine passes run in order: spacing, color, icons, copy, type, layout, details, visuals and motion. Heavy slop runs the full process. Light slop runs polish mode only, fixing what the audit found and taking the direction from the existing brand. No slop means saying so plainly and suggesting at most two or three small refinements, applied only if the user agrees. A real hero visual can be generated with an image tool when one is available. The run ends with a check against the audit list and a report of the direction, what changed per pass, and any image prompt written.

Limits as written in the SKILL.md: it does not rename the product, does not change what the product is, keeps features, content and...
